principles: One canonical structural evaluator feeds both CLI diagnostics and lifecycle admission.
PLAN evidence is declarative and verifier-derived, never executable or caller-authored.
Flat project mode is explicit and reversible; later selective applicability is not inferred.
drivers: Prevent omitted producer-consumer paths before DEV starts.
Avoid false blocks for new typed endpoints, docs-only, single-outcome and legacy stories.
Make every blocking fact mechanically registered, fresh and mutation-tested.

options.name: A: Reuse proofStory.devGateMode and integrate a canonical acceptance-topology evaluator
pros: Uses the existing flat observe/warn/enforce ownership
Keeps CLI and transition results identical
Avoids adding selective applicability before Wave 3A
cons: The existing dev gate now aggregates another structural check

options.name: B: Add a separate acceptanceTopologyMode configuration
pros: Smaller apparent coupling to existing ProofStory DEV checks
cons: Contradicts the approved flat-mode boundary unless precedence is newly designed

options.name: C: Inline topology checks only in story_advance
cons: Makes mutation and process-fact verification weaker

chosen: A: Reuse proofStory.devGateMode and integrate a canonical acceptance-topology evaluator
rationale: Wave 2 explicitly requires a flat project observe/warn/enforce structural gate. Reusing devGateMode preserves current configuration ownership, while a shared pure evaluator keeps the public command, transition gate and tests on the same semantics. Separate selective policy remains deferred to Wave 3A.

preMortem.scenario: A typed new producer-consumer declaration is rejected because symbols do not exist yet.
preMortem.trigger: Evaluator accidentally consumes current executable discovery as a PLAN requirement.
preMortem.consequence: Valid work cannot enter DEV and teams encode fake existing symbols.
preMortem.mitigation: Test planned declaration acceptance using frozen file/scope refs and assert no executable evidence is consulted.

preMortem.scenario: A partial or stale basis is presented as structurally complete.
preMortem.trigger: CLI trusts topology rows or caller status instead of verified receipt state.
preMortem.consequence: Missing paths pass the PLAN gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Derive status only from Wave 1A verification, reject caller fields, and add partial/stale/tamper mutations with stable AT codes.

preMortem.scenario: CLI diagnostics and PLAN to DEV gate disagree.
preMortem.trigger: Handler and transition orchestrator implement separate predicates.
preMortem.consequence: Operator sees PASS but story_advance blocks, or the reverse.
preMortem.mitigation: Use one canonical evaluator/result model and production-chain tests exercising both consumers.

preMortem.scenario: Legacy or docs-only work is blocked by missing topology artifacts.
preMortem.trigger: Applicability is treated as universal without compatibility classification.
preMortem.consequence: Existing Stories regress when mode is enforce.
preMortem.mitigation: Encode deterministic legacy/docs-only/single-outcome classifications and test observe, warn and enforce behavior separately.
